acceptance.criterion: guest-manager-scrolled-header.spec.ts fixed at the mechanism (private-layout.ts's onMainScroll()), all 5 Playwright projects green
acceptance.evidence: Root cause confirmed (not re-diagnosed — already root-caused by T364's and T366's reports): onMainScroll() read `this.screenChrome.head() ? false : (scrollTop > 0)`, forcing `.scrolled` false whenever a route registers a pinned head, which /guests always does. This predates hub ADR-0043 (T352): before it, headPinned/footPinned decided scroll ownership, so a pinned head implied main was overflow-y:clip and never actually scrolled, making the `false` branch inert; ADR-0043 made main /guests's real scroller (no screenScroll declared) while /guests kept its pinned head, turning the same line into a live defect. Fix: removed the screenChrome.head() branch — isScrolled now follows only `mainContent.nativeElement.scrollTop > 0`. Reproduced the pre-fix failure directly (git stash push -- private-layout.ts, then npx playwright test e2e/layout/guest-manager-scrolled-header.spec.ts): '5 failed' on iPhone SE/iPhone 12/iPhone 14/Pixel 7/Desktop Chrome, identical error to T364/T366's reports ('app-screen-header never gained .scrolled after scrolling'). After the fix (git stash pop, same command): '5 passed (7.6s)' — all 5 projects. The spec's own text/assertions were not touched; the mechanism was wrong, not the test.

You can still change that until 1 May.'; es 'Nos dijeron que no podrán venir. Aún puedes cambiar la respuesta hasta el 1 de mayo.' (3rd-person-plural reported-speech, gender-neutral); fr 'On nous a dit qu'il ne sera pas possible de venir. Vous pouvez encore modifier la réponse jusqu'au 1er mai.' (impersonal 'on'/'il', no pronoun refers to the subject's unstored gender, per hub CLAUDE.md hard rule 18(c)'s same reasoning). After: es 764, en 764, fr 764, union 764, 0 mismatched keys — 'Key-set identical: True' (comparison script re-run after the edit). delegate-edit.spec.ts: npx ng test --watch=false --include='**/delegate-edit.spec.ts' -> 7 passed (7), 0 failing (unaffected by the copy change, as expected).
